stages.title: You have been appointed Chancellor.
stages.doing: You are about to write a Budget: the taxes and the spending for the next few years.
stages.why: The [fiscal rules] limit how much you can borrow, and the [OBR](obr) checks your sums.
stages.now: Read what your three advisers have to tell you, then begin.

stages.title: Choose what to plan on
stages.doing: Pick the economic forecast you will build your Budget on, and how much [headroom] to keep in reserve.
stages.why: A rosier forecast gives you more to spend now. The [OBR](obr) will publish its own forecast later, and it will not care what you assumed.
stages.now: Choose one of the four cards and a headroom target, then confirm.

stages.title: Agree the priorities with the Prime Minister
stages.doing: Tell the Prime Minister what this Budget is for: rank up to three priorities from eight.
stages.why: The order matters. Nothing is funded yet; the ways to deliver each come next, costed one by one. The [manifesto] red lines still apply.
stages.now: Tick the priorities in the order they matter, then hear the PM read them back.

stages.title: Choose how to deliver it
stages.doing: Each priority you agreed comes with a few costed ways to deliver it, proposed by the minister responsible.
stages.why: Every option is a set of the game's levers, priced against your Budget as it stands, with the [headroom] it would leave; two that count the same money cannot both be on.
stages.now: Pick any mix; the details are one link away.

stages.title: Choose how to pay for it
stages.doing: The Director of Tax shows the gap between what you have chosen and your target, and ways to close it, grouped by who pays.
stages.why: Every option carries its badge, its [manifesto] red line and its [earliest start](earliest-start), so you see what each costs you politically.
stages.now: Pick until the gap closes, or carry it into the forecast knowingly.

stages.title: Build the package
stages.doing: The details of the taxes: every lever, one group at a time, when an option is not quite right.
stages.why: Three taxes raise most of it, and the [manifesto] fences them off. A lever that breaks a promise warns in red.
stages.now: Move what you want, then go back to the options. Chosen ones are pinned at the top of their groups.

stages.title: Build the package
stages.doing: The details of the spending: every department, programme and benefit line, when an option is not quite right.
stages.why: Day-to-day budgets are set for three years. Investment counts against the debt rule, not the day-to-day one.
stages.now: Set the departments, the [flagship] programmes, investment and welfare, then go back. Ministers will tell you what each change means.

stages.title: The OBR’s forecast arrives
stages.doing: The [OBR](obr) hands you the forecast your Budget will be judged against.
stages.why: It was fixed the day you chose your assumptions, and it may not match them. Your [headroom] can rise or fall.
stages.now: Open the envelope and see what it does to your plans.

stages.title: Make the sums add up
stages.doing: Close the gap between the [headroom] you have and the headroom you wanted.
stages.why: Every route costs something: more of the ways to pay, less of what you chose, or a thinner safety margin.
stages.now: Take the routes you can live with, then move on to the speech.

stages.title: Suggested little add-ons
stages.doing: Decide whether to add up to three small announcements to the speech, or to keep your [headroom].
stages.why: An add-on gets a headline. It is also money you no longer have in reserve, and each is priced against the Budget as it stands.
stages.now: Tick up to three. Keeping the headroom is a choice too.

stages.title: Deliver the Budget
stages.doing: Give the speech and see how your backbenchers, the markets and the public react.
stages.why: Each reaction follows from what you chose, and says which choices caused it.
stages.now: Read the speech, hear the reactions, then read the verdict.
